A.explanation: Both are energy. Since $1 \text{ N} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2}$, then $1 \text{ N m} = 1 \text{ kg m}^2 \text{ s}^{-2}$.

B.explanation: Both are momentum and impulse. Since $1 \text{ N} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2}$, then $1 \text{ N s} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$.

C.explanation: Both are power. Since $1 \text{ J} = 1 \text{ kg m}^2 \text{ s}^{-2}$, then $1 \text{ J s}^{-1} = 1 \text{ kg m}^2 \text{ s}^{-3}$.

D.explanation: They differ. $1 \text{ Pa} = 1 \text{ N m}^{-2} = 1 \text{ kg m}^{-1} \text{ s}^{-2}$, while $1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2}$ is $1 \text{ N}$.

hints: Notice each option pairs a named unit such as $\text{N m}$, $\text{N s}$, $\text{J s}^{-1}$ or $\text{Pa}$ with base units $\text{kg}$, $\text{m}$ and $\text{s}$.
Recall $1 \text{ N} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2}$ and build up $\text{J} = \text{N m}$ and $\text{Pa} = \text{N m}^{-2}$ from force times distance and force per area.
Expand the left-hand side of each pair into $\text{kg}$, $\text{m}$ and $\text{s}$ and check the powers of $\text{m}$ - one pair has an extra $\text{m}^2$ difference.
walkthrough: Start from force: from $F = ma$, $1 \text{ N} = 1 \text{ kg} \times 1 \text{ m s}^{-2} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2}$.
Check option A: work is $F \times d$, so $1 \text{ N m} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2} \times 1 \text{ m} = 1 \text{ kg m}^2 \text{ s}^{-2}$, so they match.
Check option B: impulse is $F \times t$, so $1 \text{ N s} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2} \times 1 \text{ s} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$, so they match.
Check option C: power is energy per time, so $1 \text{ J s}^{-1} = 1 \text{ kg m}^2 \text{ s}^{-2} \times 1 \text{ s}^{-1} = 1 \text{ kg m}^2 \text{ s}^{-3}$, so they match.

Check option D: pressure is force per area, so $1 \text{ Pa} = 1 \text{ N m}^{-2} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2} \times 1 \text{ m}^{-2} = 1 \text{ kg m}^{-1} \text{ s}^{-2}$, which is not $1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2}$.
Only the pair in D has different base-unit powers, with $\text{m}^{-1}$ against $\text{m}^{+1}$. This is option D
